7.0.s.en: (1) Not mixing with the pagan peoples

7.0.0.en: The Hittites: the descendants of Heth, the second of the sons of Canaan, who dwelt in scattered countries of the land of Canaan. The Girgashites: one of the tribes of the Canaanites.

7.0.1.en: The Amorites: of the descendants of Canaan; because of their importance in the land of Canaan their name was sometimes applied to all the Philistines.

7.0.2.en: The Canaanites: the descendants of Canaan, the fourth son of Ham; they dwelt in every region of the Promised Land, having scattered tribes.

7.0.3.en: The Perizzites: that is, the villagers; they are older than the Canaanites and dwelt in the north of the Promised Land. The Hivites: they dwelt in Shechem and Gibeon and at the foot of Mount Lebanon, and obtained a covenant of peace from Joshua by deceit.

7.0.4.en: The Jebusites: one of the tribes of the Canaanites, who dwelt in the region that later became the city of Jerusalem.

7.0.5.en: God demands things of them after their entering the Promised Land and God's driving out before them seven pagan peoples stronger than they.

7.0.6.en: It is to be noted that God had promised Abraham to give his descendants the inheritance of ten peoples (Gen 15:19-21), but three of them disappeared and joined others, so there were these seven peoples mentioned here.

7.1.0.en: Thou shalt utterly destroy them: you shall kill them and wipe them out.

7.1.1.en: The first demand of God upon His people when they enter the Promised Land is to kill its wicked pagan inhabitants and not have pity on them, because this is God's punishment of them for their evils in which they persisted for many years, and He uses His people as an instrument to carry out this punishment. And this is not a permission to His people to kill any person except these wicked peoples.

7.1.2.en: The second divine demand is not to make treaties with the pagans but to wipe them out as He commanded.

7.2.0.en: The third divine demand is no intermarriage between the people of God and the pagan peoples, for it would make the children of God turn aside from His worship and worship the gods of the foreign nations, and then God would punish them and destroy them, as happened in the age of the Judges.

7.2.1.en: May every person be careful when entering into marriage, and choose the one who helps him in life with God and steadfastness in the Church, that he may obtain God's blessings in his life and be delivered from many problems.

7.3.1.en: Groves: the pillars which were set up on high places and mountains, which signified the pagan gods.

7.3.2.en: But what is required of them is to demolish their altars and break their idols which they worship and remove their pillars which they set up on the mountains as a symbol of their vain gods, and to burn with fire the images they carved for their gods.

7.4.0.en: God shows the reason for His command not to mix with the pagan peoples, which is that they are a people set apart for His worship and nearer to His heart than all peoples, for they worship Him and keep away from the worship of idols and the evil lusts in which the rest of the peoples walk.

7.5.0.en: The Lord shows that He did not choose His people the children of Israel because of the greatness of their number, for on the contrary they are among the fewest of peoples, and He chose their father Abraham, who was a single individual without offspring (Gen 12:1-3), then gave him Isaac. He did not take Ishmael as a son although he had twelve sons. And Jacob and his sons who entered Egypt numbered about seventy, and by God's being with them He blessed them despite the tribulations of Egypt and its bondage.

7.6.0.en: The reasons for God's choosing His people are:

7.6.2.en: 2- His oath and covenant to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to bless their descendants; for this reason He rescued them from the bondage of Egypt and delivered them from the hand of Pharaoh, hard of heart.

7.7.0.en: God's choosing His people is a declaration of His keeping His covenant with the fathers, for He keeps His covenants throughout the generations, since the number thousand points to perfection, and He will continue to care for them on condition of their obedience to Him.

7.8.0.en: On the other hand, whoever disobeys God and rejects Him, God punishes and destroys him swiftly, that is, he meets troubles in his life on earth and then eternal destruction, for He does not give them respite beyond the length of their life on earth, and destroys them with an eternal destruction, since the length of life is very short in comparison with eternity.

7.9.0.en: Because God chose His people and loved them, they must then keep His commandments and live by them.

7.9.1.en: How great is the grace of sonship which God has given you in the sacrament of Baptism! So in order to enjoy His fatherhood and care, obey His commandments, cling to the Church and repent quickly of your sins, that you may keep your sonship to Him.

7.10.s.en: (3) The blessings of keeping the commandments

7.10.0.en: God encourages His people that if they obey His commandments, He will surely be faithful to them in keeping His covenants to their fathers, so He will give them many good things.

7.11.0.en: The Lord enumerates the blessings with which He will overwhelm His people if they choose the way of obedience and keep the commandments, and these blessings are detailed in the following three verses. In this verse the blessings include:

7.11.2.en: 2- Abundance in the good things of the land, in agricultural produce.

7.11.3.en: 3- Livestock production, and an increase of the ewes on which the abundance of offspring and milk depends.

7.12.0.en: The second kind of blessings is the exaltation of the nation above all kingdoms and communities.

7.12.1.en: He also promises them a great number and fertility in the bearing of offspring, of men and animals, for the increase in the population of the people means strength in facing the enemy and a deterrent to him, and by the fertility of the animals the people enjoy abundance of food.

7.13.0.en: Diseases: sicknesses like those with which God struck the people of Egypt, such as boils.

7.13.1.en: The third blessing is God's protection of His people from the diseases that were widespread in Egypt and which they saw with their own eyes, so the people increase in strength.

7.13.2.en: The blessings of God to His children who obey Him are countless. So do not be dazzled by the success of the wicked, for it is temporary and accompanied by turmoil, while God's blessings to you are suited to you and satisfy you and give you a peace that only the children of God obtain.

7.14.1.en: God commands them to wipe out the pagan peoples and not to have pity on them, because this is God's punishment of them; for if they spare them, they will be a trap for the people of Israel through their mixing with them and worshipping their idols.

7.15.0.en: God warns him not to fear the multitude or strength of the pagan peoples living in Canaan, but to trust in the power of God that is with him, and to remember how He rescued him from the strong bondage of Egypt by striking the Egyptians with the ten plagues, and likewise He will strike everyone who is hostile to him in the land of Canaan.

7.16.0.en: The hornets: plural of "hornet," an insect yellow and black in color.

7.16.1.en: The literal meaning points to swarms of stinging insects which God will send to harass the peoples with whom Israel will go to war, so they will be a help to him in the victory over those peoples, as in (Josh 24:12). Or God will cause them troubles and harassments as the stings of hornets cause them, so that those who remain, who were not killed by the sword, and those fleeing from the war, perish.

7.17.0.en: He reassures him that the great God dwells in their midst, so he should not fear the strength of any enemy, for it is nothing before the power of God that is with him.

7.18.0.en: God declares to His people that they will wipe out the pagan peoples gradually, because if they destroyed them all at once the land would become empty of inhabitants and be filled with wild beasts, and the land would be neglected since there would be no one to cultivate it, and it would lose its fertility. So God destroys the pagans gradually until His people multiply and possess their land, so that the land continues to flow with milk and honey.

7.19.0.en: The Lord will make them be defeated before them and will make their enemies in turmoil and anxiety before them until they and their kings are wiped out, so no one can stand against the people of God.

7.19.1.en: Joshua indeed killed thirty-one kings and took their cities (Josh 12:24), in addition to the kings whom the children of Israel killed in the age of the Judges, such as Eglon king of the Ammonites (Judg 3:20, 21) and Jabin king of the Canaanites (Judg 4:21, 24).

7.20.0.en: God also commands them to smash the idol images and burn them, whatever silver or gold is on them, and not to bring them into their houses, lest their hearts be drawn to worship them like the pagan peoples, and they defile themselves and their houses and God's punishment come upon them by their death as He destroyed the pagan peoples. Indeed He calls them to hate these idols, because God commanded that they be devoted to destruction, that is, destroyed, for their uncleanness.

7.20.1.en: Reject everything connected with sin and do not keep pictures or belongings associated with evil, lest they remind you of sin in your time of weakness and make you fall into it.

7.20.2.en: God's care in the wilderness and the punishment for forgetting Him (1) The testing of the people in the wilderness and His care for them (vv. 1-10:) "All the commandments which I command thee this day shall ye observe to do, that ye may live, and multiply, and go in and possess the land which the LORD sware unto your fathers. 2And thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no. 3And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live. 4Thy raiment waxed not old upon thee, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years. 5Thou shalt also consider in thine heart, that, as a man chasteneth his son, so the LORD thy God chasteneth thee. 6Therefore thou shalt keep the commandments of the LORD thy God, to walk in his ways, and to fear him. 7For the LORD thy God bringeth thee into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and depths that spring out of valleys and hills; 8A land of wheat, and barley, and vines, and fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of oil olive, and honey; 9A land wherein thou shalt eat bread without scarcity, thou shalt not lack any thing in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass. 10When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the LORD thy God for the good land which he hath given thee."

8.0.0.en: God declares to His people that if they keep His commandments, they will obtain His blessings in the greatness of their number, their possession of the Promised Land and their enjoyment of life with Him.

8.1.0.en: Although the way from Egypt to Canaan takes no more than a few days, God made them wander in the wilderness of Sinai 40 years to test them and discipline them, so that He might know how firmly they held to His commandments amid the hard conditions of the wilderness of Sinai; and if they succeeded, He would give them the Promised Land.

8.2.0.en: God tested His people with hunger at the beginning of their journey in Sinai, and when they were about to die, God showed His care for them and sent them manna, which continued to fall every day for 40 years, that they might know that God is the source of their life, since He gave them a delicious food strange to them, which neither they nor their fathers had known before, so that they would love God and His word and do His commandments, indeed prefer them even to their material needs such as bread; or, in other words, know that God is the source of their life by His commandments and also gives them their material needs, that is, food. Christ quoted this verse in His reply to Satan at the temptation (Mt 4:4).

8.3.0.en: In God's care for His people in the harsh conditions of the wilderness of Sinai, He preserved their clothes so that they did not wear out for 40 years. This is beyond the ability of ordinary cloth to endure for all this time. And He gave their feet strength so that they did not swell from so much walking on the sands of the wilderness and on its mountains. So God, along with the commandment, gives help to make us feel His presence and encourage us to carry out His commandments.

8.4.0.en: God shows that His discipline of His people by their wandering in the wilderness of Sinai 40 years was not vengeance or cruelty but care and concern, as a father cares for the upbringing of his son and his discipline so that he may be a strong and successful person.

8.4.1.en: Look at God's care and providence for you, and accept His disciplines in the form of the adverse circumstances you meet in your life, for they are for your good and for correcting your mistakes, and this impels you to repentance and to thanking God for His love.

8.5.0.en: In view of God's fatherhood and great love, His children must hold fast to His commandments with all exactness and fear Him in their works, so that they walk uprightly.

8.6.0.en: Depths: the abundant waters that come out of the springs in addition to rainwater. Valleys: the wadis and the various places of the land.

8.6.1.en: He gives them the good news that the land they will possess enjoys abundant water, which helps its cultivation and fertility and the abundance of the crops it produces.

8.7.0.en: He mentions a proof of the fertility of the land, which is the variety of its great crops such as wheat and barley, in addition to fruits such as grapes, figs, pomegranates and olives, and likewise it has bees and abundant honey.

8.8.0.en: Without scarcity: you will eat sparingly for fear of the scarcity of its fruits.

8.8.1.en: God gives them the good news of abundant crops, so they eat of them as they wish, in addition to the presence in it of mines of metals such as iron and copper.

8.9.0.en: After they obtain these good things, they must thank God and bless Him; this is the natural response to God's grace.

8.9.1.en: (2) Not forgetting God (vv. 11-16:) "11Beware that thou forget not the LORD thy God, in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command thee this day: 12Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein; 13And when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied; 14Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the LORD thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; 15Who led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint; 16Who fed thee in the wilderness with manna, which thy fathers knew not, that he might humble thee, and that he might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end;"

8.10.0.en: Before Moses enumerates to them the reasons that may make them turn aside from the Law, he repeats his warning to the people of the necessity of holding fast to the commandment and the judgments and statutes which he charges them with.

8.11.0.en: He warns them against forgetting God and His worship through preoccupation with the good things of the land, which are:

8.11.2.en: 2- Settling in houses and fortified cities.

8.12.0.en: God reminds them of His care for them throughout their journey in the harsh wilderness of Sinai, where He preserved them from the poisonous serpents widespread in the mountains and from scorpions and protected them from the terrors of the land. And despite the dryness of the wilderness of Sinai, God gave them water from the hard flint rocks from which water cannot come, and He also gave them manna from heaven; and although He allowed them to suffer and be humbled so that they would feel the hardship of life, as a result of disobeying God's commandments, at the same time He showed them His kindnesses to them in preserving them and providing for their needs of food and drink, so that they would believe in Him and trust in Him and obey His commandments, to possess in the end the Promised Land and then enter the Kingdom of Heaven after their earthly life.

8.12.1.en: Beware of being preoccupied with material things instead of God, but thank God for them and use them in measure and remember that they are God's grace to you, so that you take them with thanksgiving and also do not forget His care for you throughout your life.

8.12.2.en: (3) Pride and the punishment of forgetting (vv. 17-20:) "17Lest thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth. 18But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day. 19And it shall be, if thou do at all forget the LORD thy God, and walk after other gods, and serve them, and worship them, I testify against you this day that ye shall surely perish. 20As the nations which the LORD destroyeth before your face, so shall ye perish; because ye would not be obedient unto the voice of the LORD your God."

8.13.0.en: God warns them not to attribute the good things of the land of Canaan to their own power, in pride and arrogance, when they become rich through the abundance of their possessions.

8.14.0.en: God calls them to remember Him in prayer, because He is the giver of good things, as He promised their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

8.14.1.en: Thank God every day for His gifts, so your love for Him appears and His blessings overflow upon you. And enjoy the gifts of His that are in your hands, so you live in joy however many tribulations surround you, and spread joy among others, especially those who suffer tribulations.

8.15.0.en: God warns them that if they leave Him and worship idols and neglect His commandments, He will wipe them out and destroy them.

8.16.0.en: God gives them an example for guarding against the worship of idols, namely the pagan peoples living in the land of Canaan, whom God will wipe out from before them because of their worship of idols.
